learning: Iteration 1 showed that kp 3.0 with base_speed 1.4 gave more oscillation and a larger max_error than iteration 0 at kp 2.5. This iteration tests whether the 16 mm footprint removes line loss while a lower kp and higher kd keep max_error under 0.06 m. If line_loss_events is still above zero, the footprint alone is not enough and the span or y position must change next.
notes: Builder's 16 mm footprint on the same seven-sensor array, with a damped controller: kp lowered to 2.5, kd raised to 0.20, base_speed lowered to 1.3. Iteration 1 showed kp 3.0 raised oscillation to 0.186 and max_error to 0.068 m, so this tests whether less gain and more damping keep the robot on the line.
rationale: Iteration 1 raced zero finishes. All 60 trials ended off_track, with line_loss_events of 2 on the oval and 1 on the S-bend and slalom, and max_error of 0.064 to 0.068 m. That is worse than iteration 0 (max_error about 0.061 m), and steering_oscillation rose from about 0.075 to 0.186 when kp went from 2.5 to 3.0 and base_speed fell. So the higher kp is likely overshooting and adding oscillation, not helping. The Builder's iteration 2 geometry changes only the sensor footprint, from 12 mm to 16 mm, so I keep the sensor positions, the 0.10 m track, the 0.7 kg mass and body_width 0.12 m fixed. A 16 mm footprint (half-size 8 mm) lets each sensor see tape out to a centre offset of about 20.5 mm, against about 18.5 mm at 12 mm, and it makes the adjacent footprints overlap more at 10 mm pitch. That should reduce the line-loss events on the oval and S-bend. For the controller I keep the outer-weighted sensor scaling, which is monotonic across the span, but reduce kp from 3.0 to 2.5 to damp the oscillation seen in iteration 1, and raise kd from 0.15 to 0.20 to add damping against the short lookahead at y = 0.04 m. I reduce base_speed from 1.4 to 1.3 so the robot has more time to correct on the bends where max_error peaked. ki stays at 0.05 to remove small motor-mismatch bias and remains well inside its limit. line_loss stays at last_direction. Expected result: line_loss_events at or near 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and the first completions on the oval or S-bend. Whether the lower speed still allows a 3 s finish is untested, so the next race's completion_time will show it.
